ctime_compare.instructions: Does `hunk` add or change code that compares file timestamps (st_ctime, st_mtime, st_ctime_ns, st_mtime_ns, getmtime, getctime or another st_* time field) taken at different times or from different stat calls, to decide whether a file changed? Count timestamps placed in a cache key, identity or fingerprint tuple that is compared later. Windows gives these fields different meanings.

criteria.true: an added or changed line puts a stat time field into a comparison, cache key, fingerprint or identity used to detect change
criteria.false: no stat time field is used for change detection (absent, only printed, or only set with os.utime)

posix_only.instructions: Does `hunk` add behaviour that works only on Linux/macOS or differs on Windows: file-system path strings split, matched or compared on a literal '/', os.fork, fcntl, signal handlers or SIGALRM/SIGKILL, chmod or executable-bit assumptions, os.getuid, /tmp or /dev paths, POSIX shell commands, or file names that differ only by case?

criteria.true: an added line relies on one of those behaviours without a platform guard
criteria.false: no added line relies on POSIX-only behaviour (pathlib joins and os.path calls are portable), or it is guarded by an explicit platform check

pinned_value.instructions: Does `hunk` replace a pinned expected value: a removed (-) line holds a count literal that a test or gate asserts, a SHA-256 digest, a byte offset or address, a size, or a golden / reference value, and an added (+) line holds a different value in its place?

criteria.true: an old expected count, digest, offset, size or golden value on a - line is replaced by a different one on a + line
criteria.false: no expected value is replaced; brand-new code or new tests that only add assertions do not count

slow_test.instructions: Does `hunk` add or lengthen a test path that could run for minutes: nested loops over a large case matrix or cross product (see the loop facts in `file_facts`), sleeps or polling waits, full disc / ISO / XBE builds or scans, or many repeated heavy calls such as a full prepare/build/read-back per case? CI kills a test file after 420 seconds.

criteria.true: added test code runs hundreds of heavy cases (each a build, prepare, read-back, compress, fit or render), sleeps, full-disc work, or other heavy repeated calls
criteria.false: the added code is not a test path, or its loops are small, or the loop body is only cheap assignments or arithmetic (fast even with thousands of iterations)

weakens_safety.instructions: Does `hunk` widen or weaken a safety check? Safety checks are: validation of files, saves or user input, refusals and raised errors, integrity checks (hashes, signatures, sizes, bounds), path and permission guards, allowlists, and test assertions. Weakening means removing one, loosening its condition or tolerance, adding a skip or bypass, or making it accept inputs it used to refuse.

criteria.true: a safety check of that kind is removed, loosened, skipped or bypassed, or now accepts inputs it used to refuse
criteria.false: safety checks are unchanged, added or stricter; feature conditions, performance paths, search heuristics, cache bookkeeping and early returns that only skip work are not safety checks

inventory_mismatch.instructions: Does `hunk` touch the release inventory or pins without the matching change: it adds or imports a module that `diff_facts` marks MISSING from the release allowlist or not in module_pins, or it edits an allowlist, requirements, module_pins entry or pinned count while `diff_facts` says the counterpart was not edited?

criteria.true: the hunk adds, imports or edits something whose allowlist entry, pin or count `diff_facts` marks MISSING or not edited
criteria.false: `diff_facts` shows every matching change present, or the hunk touches no inventory, pin or new module
